newsitem.title: INDIA: India base metals market closed for Hindu festival.
newsitem.headline: India base metals market closed for Hindu festival.

text.p: The Bombay Metals Exchange was closed on Wednesday for a Hindu festival. Trading resumes on Thursday.
On Tuesday tin and nickel prices fell while other base metals were steady in limited trade.

Tin and nickel dropped further on improved arrivals of imported metals while local traders turned sellers following a subdued world trend. Tin fell 200 rupees to 31,000 rupees per quintal and nickel 300 rupees to 36,000 rupees per quintal.
Industrial buyers kept to the sidelines and sentiment was subdued at close. On Monday tin and nickel were down 200 rupees each per quintal.

Copper lost 25 rupees to 13,500 rupees under selling pressure, triggered by a downtrend in world prices. Zinc was steady at 7,850 rupees. Lead was unchanged at 4,550 rupees and aluminium was quiet at 7,450 rupees per quintal.
